new_statements.quote: 彝语中的每个音节都有声调。但各地的声调数量多少不等,一般有3-5个声调。彝语南部方言双柏话有高平、中平、低降三个声调。彝语除了有声调外,有些音节还带有表意重音或表情重音。重音是相连的音节中某个音节发音突出的现象,它出现在句子中,同时也出现在某些语言的单词中。如云南双柏彝语: do21 lo55 ve33 “得了!”或“够了!”(看见异常情况时所发出来的自然感叹声或紧急呼声) 凉山彝语 ... mo33 “阿妈!”(遇到危险时的惊呼声) 这类摹描自然声响的象声词和叹词,都带表意重音或表情重音。另外,彝语的表意重音有区别词汇意义和语法意义的作用。
new_statements.translation: Every syllable in Yi carries a tone, though the number of tones varies from place to place, generally 3-5. Shuangbai speech of the Southern Yi dialect has three tones: high level, mid level and low falling. Besides tone, some syllables in Yi also carry 'semantic stress' or 'expressive stress'. Stress is the phenomenon whereby one syllable among adjacent syllables is pronounced with prominence; it occurs in sentences and also in the words of some languages. E.g. Shuangbai Yi (Yunnan) do21 lo55 ve33 'Enough!/That will do!' (a spontaneous exclamation or urgent cry on seeing something unusual), Liangshan Yi ... mo33 'Mother!' (a cry of alarm in danger): onomatopoeic words and interjections of this kind all carry semantic or expressive stress. Moreover, semantic stress in Yi serves to distinguish lexical and grammatical meanings.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Syllable-tone language (three tones on every syllable); no fixed word-stress position is stated. The source recognises an additional, non-positional 'semantic/expressive stress' that makes particular syllables prominent (interjections, onomatopoeia, and lexically/grammatically contrastive cases), i.e. stress is treated as a sporadic lexical-expressive feature layered on tone, not as a predictable word-level accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Interjections and onomatopoeic words always carry expressive/semantic stress; semantic stress said to distinguish lexical and grammatical meaning (details not visible in the snippets).
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is framed for Yi / the Southern Yi dialect in general and exemplified with Shuangbai speech (E-Xin vernacular = Northern Nisu [yiv] in ISO/Yang 2009 terms), not with a Southern Nisu [nsd] datapoint; stress is described as occurring 'in sentences and also in some words'. Accessed as Google Books snippets only, not full pages. The one description whose datapoint is S Nisu proper (Wang Chengyou 2003, Nisu chapter: 'every syllable has a fixed tone') shows no stress passage in snippet search.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted stress passage (Li 1996) describes Yi / the 'Southern Yi dialect' generically and is exemplified with Shuangbai speech (E-Xin vernacular = Northern/Northwestern Nisu, ISO yiv, Glottolog nort2718), not with a Southern Nisu [nsd] datapoint. The accessible surveys that do include [nsd] datapoints (Yang 2009: Honghe Baohe, Yuanyang Shalatuo/Shengcun, Jinping Jinhe, Yuanjiang Longtan, Shiping Niujie; Lama 2012: Jiangcheng) are silent on stress. Wang Chengyou 2003's Nisu chapter (Yuanyang per Glottolog / Honghe per Yang 2009) is the [nsd]-proper description but is print-only. 'Dali Nisu' of Yang & Yang 2018 is the Far Northwestern Nisu area (farn1234), a different language.

sources.note: pp. 14-15 (phonology intro, illustrated with Shuangbai = E-Xin vernacular, i.e. Northern Nisu [yiv]): every Yi syllable has a tone (Shuangbai: high level, mid level, low falling); in addition some syllables carry 'semantic stress' (表意重音) or 'expressive stress' (表情重音), i.e. prominence of one syllable among adjacent syllables, occurring in sentences and in some words (interjections, onomatopoeia); semantic stress can distinguish lexical and grammatical meaning. tone.says: Nisu has FOUR tones, values 55, 33, 22, 21 (example words lA55 'dig out', lu33 'shake', dA22 'draw out', gA21 'flick'); low-falling 21 is realised 31 with a final glottal stop after tense vowels; mid-level 33 is realised 44 after tense vowels; a further note on how the Chinese 51 tone is borrowed in early vs recent loans (cut off). Tense/lax contrast on 14 of 17 monophthongs, occurring 'on all tones'. This differs from Yang 2009 / Lama 2012 (three tonemes 55/33/21) by splitting a 22 tone.
